newsitem.title: USA: MCI says merger chance to leapfrog rivals.
newsitem.headline: MCI says merger chance to leapfrog rivals.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp Chairman Bert Roberts said on Tuesday that the company's planned merger with British Telecommunications Plc was a chance to leapfrog competitors vying to establish a global presence.

Roberts and BT Chairman Sir Iain Vallance promoted the benefits of the proposed $20 billion merger at a news conference in San Francisco, saying the companies would be pooling their strengths at a time when telecommunications markets around the world are opening to competition.

"MCI has broken the mold of the American telecommunications market and BT has broken the mold of the European market. Together, I'm quite confident that we will break the mold of the global market," Vallance said.

Roberts said that joining the two companies now "gives us the opportunity to leapfrog much of our competition, to get out in front of people that we will be competing with to establish a presence around the world...while we remain strong in our own markets."

Roberts said the companies remained confident they would close the proposed merger in the fall of this year. The plan for the new company, to be called Concert Plc, must be approved by shareholders and by regulators in Europe and the United States.
Vallance said the European Commission had to decide on the merger by the end of May. "I don't think there's going to be any significant roadblock there," he said.
Roberts said he expected the U.S. Federal Communications Commission to rule on the proposed merger "some time during the summer".
"I think I can say I'm optimistic about it," he said.

Talking about BT's business, Vallance said the company was "getting ready for what amounts to the opportunity of a lifetime as the European telecommunications market opens up to full competition at the beginning of January next year."
"We're well positioned not only in the big markets of Germany and France but also in Holland, Italy, Spain and Scandinavia," he said.
Vallance praised the global telecommunications trade agreement reached in Geneva on Saturday intended to open telecommunications markets to competition.
"In a sense, it fulfills some of the ambitions that lie behind the merger of BT and MCI, because we were probably the two companies to see it coming earliest," he said.
"There has been customer demand for the globalization of telecommunications for a long while...and now we are seeing a major step towards it," he added.
